sources.citation: Dimmendaal, Gerrit J. 2012. Metrical structures: A neglected property of Nilotic (and other African language families). Author's master copy PDF, Univ. Cologne (held held by the project under catalog nand1266)
sources.note: Kalenjin section (§4.1) uses Nandi data only; cites Rottland 1982:78 solely for the north-south decrease in vowel length across Kalenjin; no Sabaot/Elgon stress statement.

sources.citation: Rottland, Franz. 1982. Die Südnilotischen Sprachen: Beschreibung, Vergleichung und Rekonstruktion (Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 7). Berlin: Reimer. Table of contents (Rosetta Project excerpt, archive.org rosettaproject_spy_contents-1)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number AFR.EAST. R 749 s; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.N5 R68x1982)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number AFR.EAST. R 749 s; Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.N5 R68x1982
sources.note: TOC only: under '5. Kalenjin / 5.1 Phonologie' it lists '5.1.3 Prosodische Erscheinungen 1. Länge 2. Druckakzent 3. Ton.. 77' and '5.2.3 Prosodische Erscheinungen 1. Länge 2. Ton.. 85'; the Druckakzent (stress) section itself (pp. 77-78) is not in the excerpt.

sources.citation: Machani, Kebeya et al. 2022. Core/Cultural Borrowing in Sabaot from Kiswahili. International Journal of Linguistics Studies 2(2). doi:10.32996/ijls.2022.2.2.13
sources.note: Lexical borrowing only; no phonology section and no Sabaot phonology references in its bibliography.

sources.citation: Chemorion, Diphus Chosefu. 2008. Translating Jonah's narration and poetry into Sabaot: towards a participatory approach to Bible translation (PABT). DTh thesis, Stellenbosch University (handle 10019.1/1094)
sources.note: §4.4.3.2 pp. 94-95: Sabaot orthography (SIL/Sabaot Language Committee, approved 1988) 'has very special features for marking grammatical tones'; 13 consonants, 20 vowels citing Kipkirich & Larsen 2006:2-4, 18-19. Nothing on stress (the only 'stress' hit is Nord's general text-analysis model).

sources.citation: Lodge, Ken. 1995. Kalenjin phonology and morphology. Lingua 96: 29-43 (held held by the project under catalog nand1266)
sources.note: Tugen dialect; lists 'Mount Elgon speakers: Sapiny, Kany, Terik, Pok, Pong'om' as a Kalenjin grouping; ATR harmony only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.). 1993. Alphabets of Africa. Dakar: UNESCO/SIL, p. 188 'Kenya: Sabaot (Southern Nilotic)' (Rosetta Project scan)
sources.note: Phoneme/orthography chart; 'Tone: Tone markers before the word shows grammatical tone distinctions' (subject vs non-subject noun tone, indefinite subject, 2nd vs 3rd person, future vs negative non-past, emphatic); stress not mentioned.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE, Sabaot (saba1262) inventory 'sabaot (AA 812)' = Hartell 1993 Alphabets of Africa
sources.note: 31-segment inventory derived from the Alphabets of Africa page; no tone or stress information.

sources.citation: Rottland 1982, pp. 22-23 (Elgon-Zweig: Kony, Pok, Bong'om, Terik) and pp. 20-22 (Sapiny; Nandi, Kipsikiis, Keyo, Tuken) — Rosetta Project excerpt pages
sources.note: Ethnographic/geographic sections only (names, self-designations, settlement); nothing on stress or tone.
